text:
**My pick for most people is the JBL Charge 6.** It's rated IP68 (dust-tight, survives submersion) and gets 20 hours of battery, or 28 with Playtime Boost. What Hi-Fi named it best overall, and prices there run about $130 at Walmart to $150 at Amazon ([What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)). BestProducts also ranks it first, praising the sound, the tough build, and its use as a power bank ([BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)).

**Other good options by need**

- **Pool party, loudest and floats: JBL Boombox 4.** RTINGS' top waterproof pick. It handles long immersion, floats, and runs over 40 hours. The sound is narrow, so it's best when you're in front of it ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)).
- **Even sound all around the pool: Ultimate Ears EPICBOOM.** It's IP67, floats, and has a 360-degree design, with about 15 hours of battery. It's Tom's Guide's best overall and RTINGS' best mid-range pick ([Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers), [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)).
- **Easy to carry to the beach: JBL Grip, about $100.** It's IP68, weighs under a pound, and is the size of a drink can. Battery life is 12 hours. Good Housekeeping's DJ tester picked it as best overall, though the mesh body can trap dust ([Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)).
- **Budget: Ultimate Ears WONDERBOOM 4, about $65.** It's IP67, floats, and has 360-degree sound with 14 hours of battery ([BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)). For something cheaper and tiny, the JBL Go 5 (IP67, about $40) is What Hi-Fi's budget pick, but it only gets 8 hours of battery ([What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)).
- **Big sound with a built-in light show: Soundcore Boom 2 Plus.** It's 100 W, IPX7, floats, and gets up to 20 hours at half volume. The list price is $249.99, or about $200 with code AFSC20 at Soundcore's store. The site that tested the code says it worked in Soundcore's cart on 2026-10-22, and the code expires 2026-12-31. It weighs 3.8 kg (about 8.4 lb), and the 20 hours assumes BassUp and lights are off. [Buy at Soundcore](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus). This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-boom-2-plus)).

**Care tips**

- IP ratings don't cover damage from salt or chlorine. RTINGS suggests rinsing the speaker with fresh water after use ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)).
- For sandy beaches, look for a dust rating (the first number, like IP67 or IP68). Speakers rated IPX7 only, or the Boom 2 with no dust rating, are better kept on a towel ([BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)).
- Keep the charging port flap closed, and let the speaker dry fully before charging.

The review pages above have retailer buttons for the JBL and Ultimate Ears models, since I don't have direct product links for them. Prices change, so check the current price at checkout.

If you tell me your budget and whether you want portable or party-loud, I can narrow this to one pick.
